findings.issue_text: Search index misses events written during index build because initWatcher now runs after s.search.init, creating a window where writes between index snapshot and watcher start are never indexed (server.go:300-308)

Eager Init in NewResourceServer uses caller-supplied context for watcher/search background goroutines, which will be torn down if a request-scoped or cancellable context is passed, silently stopping event ingestion (server.go:258-262)
Eager init makes initialization failure fatal at construction time (returns nil, err), blocking startup on slow index build and hard-failing callers with degraded-mode fallbacks (server.go:258-262)

BuildIndex no longer serializes cache writes vs. concurrent builds after removing the whole-build cacheMu lock, allowing duplicate full-table builds and callers to hold different ResourceIndex instances causing inconsistent search results (bleve.go:85-88, 137-140)
Postgres integration test is skipped, dropping CI coverage of the production-like DB path for the very code changed in this PR (eager Init, watcher/search ordering) (module_server_test.go:35-38)

Concurrent duplicate index builds in BuildIndex after removing the coarse lock: two requests for the same (namespace, resource, group) key can both run the full builder and one result silently overwrites the other in the cache, roughly doubling peak memory for in-memory indices and potentially erroring for file-backed indices due to concurrent bleve.New on the same path; needs a per-key singleflight/in-progress map (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:85-140)

Synchronous full index build moved into the constructor path: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) inline, blocking process startup on a full reindex of every namespaced resource before the server can serve health checks or blob reads, with no timeout or partial-failure isolation (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:255-261, search.go:170-216)

Postgres integration test skipped with 'not working in Drone' (module_server_test.go:35-38), leaving the most production-relevant DB path with zero integration coverage, exactly where the init-reordering and constructor-time Init changes are riskiest

Behavioral change: eager Init in NewResourceServer removes lazy-init error handling from every RPC; a failed init now permanently fails construction and no tests were added for init error propagation, RPC behavior without manual Init, or double-init prevention
Reordering: search index init now happens before watcher init, so writes landing between index snapshot and watcher start are lost from the index; no test covers writes during init being indexed

Postgres integration test in pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35-38 is skipped with a TODO instead of fixed, leaving the PR's eager-init behavioral change with zero postgres integration coverage and potentially masking a failure caused by this PR

Removed global cache mutex from BuildIndex disk path (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:85-137): concurrent builds for the same key can race on bleve.New(dir, ...) for the same directory, and concurrent cache lookups can trigger duplicate builds; no concurrency test added

History and Origin no longer guard against nil/uninitialized s.search while Search retains a nil check, so a server without search configured will panic on History/Origin; no test covers calling History/Origin on a server without search

New TotalDocs() call in the init log line (pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:213-216, 277-280) may be unsafe or hit a nil aggregate for some backends, causing init to fail at startup; no test asserts init succeeds with the added logging across backend configurations

Race on b.cache map read in bleveBackend.BuildIndex: the cache lookup at the top of the function is now performed without cacheMu while other goroutines write the map under cacheMu, risking a fatal concurrent map read and write and duplicate index builds

Removing the full-function lock in BuildIndex allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same file-backed index: two concurrent bleve.New calls on the same directory are not serialized, so one build fails and the old per-key singleflight guarantee is gone

initWatcher now runs after search index build, so DB writes landing during the (potentially minutes-long) build window fire events before the watcher is subscribed and are permanently lost from the index, returning stale/missing search results

Eager Init in NewResourceServer changes failure semantics: a single transient init failure now permanently fails construction with no retry, and the constructor-scoped ctx may be short-lived/canceled and abort the long index build
Postgres integration test is skipped with a silent-pass guard, potentially hiding a regression this PR introduced rather than fixing it

With Init no longer called at request time, Search/History/Origin can nil-pointer or operate on an uninitialized search support if constructed via a path without eager Init, and duplicate/misleading error logs can occur, giving callers less precise errors

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Search index misses events written during index build because initWatcher now runs after s.search.init, creating a window where writes between index snapshot and watcher start are never indexed (server.go:300-308)

adjudication.rationale: In server.Init the order was changed so the search index is initialized before starting the watcher (server.go: search.init(ctx) now runs before s.initWatcher()). This is a concrete behavioral change that could create a gap where writes occurring during/after the index build aren’t observed by the watcher. However, the diff doesn’t show how s.search.init snapshots data or how initWatcher subscribes (e.g., whether it replays from a cursor/offset), so the claim that events are *definitely* missed can’t be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Eager Init in NewResourceServer uses caller-supplied context for watcher/search background goroutines, which will be torn down if a request-scoped or cancellable context is passed, silently stopping event ingestion (server.go:258-262)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows NewResourceServer now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` (server.go ~255-262) and removes per-RPC `Init(ctx)` calls. `Init` passes that `ctx` into `s.search.init(ctx)` (server.go ~300-307), and `search.init` uses the context (at least for tracing spans after the change to `ctx, span := ...`). While the claim that watcher/search background goroutines will be “torn down” and “silently stop ingestion” is not directly verifiable from the shown diff (e.g., `initWatcher()` takes no ctx here, and the diff doesn’t show goroutines tied to ctx cancellation), it is a concrete lifecycle/architecture concern that initialization now depends on whatever `ctx` is in scope in the constructor, which could be cancellable depending on how it’s sourced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Eager init makes initialization failure fatal at construction time (returns nil, err), blocking startup on slow index build and hard-failing callers with degraded-mode fallbacks (server.go:258-262)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make initialization eager and fatal at construction time: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure (server.go ~255-262), while per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc. Since `Init` can run `s.search.init(ctx)` (server.go ~300-309), which may be expensive (index creation), this can block server creation/startup and prevents constructing the server in a partially functional/degraded mode. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove this is an outright defect—it's a behavior/architecture change whose appropriateness depends on intended startup semantics and fallback design not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BuildIndex no longer serializes cache writes vs. concurrent builds after removing the whole-build cacheMu lock, allowing duplicate full-table builds and callers to hold different ResourceIndex instances causing inconsistent search results (bleve.go:85-88, 137-140)
matched_golden_ids: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that removing the full-function cacheMu lock in BuildIndex allows concurrent goroutines to perform duplicate expensive index builds for the same key, resulting in multiple index instances. This is the same race/duplication issue described in the golden comment caused by narrowing the lock to only the final cache assignment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Postgres integration test is skipped, dropping CI coverage of the production-like DB path for the very code changed in this PR (eager Init, watcher/search ordering) (module_server_test.go:35-38)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a conditional skip for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with the comment that it’s not working in Drone (module_server_test.go). This reduces CI coverage for Postgres specifically while the PR also changes initialization behavior (eager `Init` in `NewResourceServer` and reorders watcher/search init), so the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded testing/coverage concern rather than a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Concurrent duplicate index builds in BuildIndex after removing the coarse lock: two requests for the same (namespace, resource, group) key can both run the full builder and one result silently overwrites the other in the cache, roughly doubling peak memory for in-memory indices and potentially erroring for file-backed indices due to concurrent bleve.New on the same path; needs a per-key singleflight/in-progress map (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:85-140)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function (including bleve.New/NewMemOnly and the builder call). The diff removes that coarse lock and only locks around the final cache write (b.cache[key] = idx). With this change, concurrent calls to BuildIndex for the same key can both proceed to create/build an index and then one will overwrite the other in the cache. For file-backed indices, both could call bleve.New on the same dir path (derived from key), which can lead to errors/races; for in-memory indices it can roughly double peak memory. The diff shows no per-key in-progress coordination to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Synchronous full index build moved into the constructor path: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) inline, blocking process startup on a full reindex of every namespaced resource before the server can serve health checks or blob reads, with no timeout or partial-failure isolation (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:255-261, search.go:170-216)

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly moves initialization into the constructor path: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if init fails (server.go:255-261). `Init` invokes `s.search.init(ctx)` before starting the watcher (server.go:300-312), and `searchSupport.init` is explicitly described as blocking startup on failure and appears to perform index initialization work (search.go:170-216). This means server construction can now block on search initialization and can fail server creation entirely, which can delay/avoid serving endpoints (including health/blob RPCs) compared to the prior lazy per-RPC `Init` calls that were removed. The claim about “full reindex of every namespaced resource” is plausible but not fully verifiable from the shown diff, so the core issue is the synchronous init/blocking constructor behavior rather than the exact scope of reindexing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Postgres integration test skipped with 'not working in Drone' (module_server_test.go:35-38), leaving the most production-relevant DB path with zero integration coverage, exactly where the init-reordering and constructor-time Init changes are riskiest

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a Postgres-specific skip in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (`if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip("...not working with postgres in Drone") }`), which removes integration coverage for Postgres in CI. In the same PR, `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` at construction time and `Init` ordering changes in `server.go`, increasing risk around initialization behavior; skipping Postgres means the most production-relevant DB path won’t exercise these changes in integration tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change: eager Init in NewResourceServer removes lazy-init error handling from every RPC; a failed init now permanently fails construction and no tests were added for init error propagation, RPC behavior without manual Init, or double-init prevention

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (server.go), and the prior per-RPC lazy init checks (`if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }`) were removed from many RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). This is a meaningful behavioral/contract change (init errors now prevent construction rather than surfacing on first RPC). The diff does not add any tests covering this new behavior (init error propagation at construction, RPC behavior without explicit Init calls, or ensuring init is only performed once), so the “no tests were added for this change” aspect is a specific, diff-grounded review concern rather than a proven correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reordering: search index init now happens before watcher init, so writes landing between index snapshot and watcher start are lost from the index; no test covers writes during init being indexed

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization in `server.Init`: search index init (`s.search.init(ctx)`) is now performed before starting the watcher (`s.initWatcher()`), whereas previously the watcher started first. That reordering is real and could create a window where changes occur after the index build but before the watcher is active, potentially leaving the index stale. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove that writes are definitively “lost” (it depends on how `search.init` and `initWatcher` coordinate RVs/checkpoints), and the diff doesn’t show tests around this timing either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Postgres integration test in pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35-38 is skipped with a TODO instead of fixed, leaving the PR's eager-init behavioral change with zero postgres integration coverage and potentially masking a failure caused by this PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a TODO and skips the integration test when dbType == "postgres" in pkg/server/module_server_test.go (lines added around the shown hunk), reducing postgres integration coverage. In the same PR, resource server initialization behavior changes to eager-init in NewResourceServer (server.go adds `err := s.Init(ctx)` and removes per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls). Skipping postgres here can plausibly mask regressions in that new init path for postgres-backed runs, making this a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed global cache mutex from BuildIndex disk path (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:85-137): concurrent builds for the same key can race on bleve.New(dir, ...) for the same directory, and concurrent cache lookups can trigger duplicate builds; no concurrency test added

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, the diff removes the cacheMu lock that previously covered the entire BuildIndex call (including bleve.New(dir, mapper)/bleve.NewMemOnly) and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This change makes it possible for two concurrent BuildIndex calls (if they happen) to build the same key simultaneously and both attempt to create/open the same on-disk directory index (`dir := filepath.Join(...); bleve.New(dir, mapper)`), and also allows duplicate work before the cache is populated. However, the diff does not show whether higher layers serialize builds per key, so the race/duplicate-build scenario is a grounded concern but not strictly verifiable as a definite defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: History and Origin no longer guard against nil/uninitialized s.search while Search retains a nil check, so a server without search configured will panic on History/Origin; no test covers calling History/Origin on a server without search

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go, Search still checks `if s.search == nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("search index not configured") }`, but History and Origin now directly call `return s.search.History(ctx, req)` and `return s.search.Origin(ctx, req)` with no nil check. Since Init() only initializes search when `s.search != nil` and otherwise does not error, a ResourceServer constructed without search configured could still have `s.search == nil` and History/Origin would panic on nil dereference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New TotalDocs() call in the init log line (pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:213-216, 277-280) may be unsafe or hit a nil aggregate for some backends, causing init to fail at startup; no test asserts init succeeds with the added logging across backend configurations

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new log line in searchSupport.init: `s.log.Info("search index initialized", ..., "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())`. `init` is only called from server.Init when `s.search != nil` (see `if s.initErr == nil && s.search != nil { s.initErr = s.search.init(ctx) }`), so the added call is not a new obvious nil-deref at that level. The claim that `TotalDocs()` may be unsafe or hit a nil aggregate for some backends is not verifiable from this diff (no `TotalDocs()` implementation or backend behavior shown), and the referenced line ranges include unrelated code. The “no test asserts init succeeds…” portion is generic and not tied to any shown failing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race on b.cache map read in bleveBackend.BuildIndex: the cache lookup at the top of the function is now performed without cacheMu while other goroutines write the map under cacheMu, risking a fatal concurrent map read and write and duplicate index builds

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, the diff removes the broad `b.cacheMu.Lock()/Unlock()` that previously covered the whole `BuildIndex` function, and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. If `BuildIndex` still performs a cache lookup (e.g., `idx := b.cache[key]`) in unchanged code near the top, that read would now be unprotected while writes remain protected, which can cause a Go fatal "concurrent map read and map write" and allow duplicate concurrent index builds. The diff itself doesn’t show the cache read, so the race is plausible but not directly verifiable from the shown hunks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the full-function lock in BuildIndex allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same file-backed index: two concurrent bleve.New calls on the same directory are not serialized, so one build fails and the old per-key singleflight guarantee is gone

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function (b.cacheMu.Lock()/defer Unlock()), which serialized concurrent calls. The diff removes that full-function lock and now only locks around writing b.cache[key] = idx. This means two goroutines can concurrently miss the cache and both proceed to create a file-backed index for the same key, calling bleve.New(dir, mapper) on the same directory without serialization. The diff shows no replacement singleflight/per-key guard here, so duplicate concurrent builds are now possible and can cause build failures/corruption depending on bleve's directory creation semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: initWatcher now runs after search index build, so DB writes landing during the (potentially minutes-long) build window fire events before the watcher is subscribed and are permanently lost from the index, returning stale/missing search results

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go, Init() now calls s.search.init(ctx) before s.initWatcher() (order swapped from the prior code). If the watcher is the mechanism that subscribes to/receives WrittenEvent updates used to keep the search index current, then any writes occurring while s.search.init (potentially long-running index build) is executing would happen before the watcher subscription exists and thus would not be observed for incremental indexing. The diff shows the exact reordering that enables this missed-update window; whether those events are replayed/caught up is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Eager Init in NewResourceServer changes failure semantics: a single transient init failure now permanently fails construction with no retry, and the constructor-scoped ctx may be short-lived/canceled and abort the long index build

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows NewResourceServer now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), while all per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed. This changes semantics from lazy/possibly retryable initialization (each request could attempt init again) to “fail construction and never serve” on any init error, which could matter if init can fail transiently. However, the claim that the constructor-scoped `ctx` is short-lived/canceled and would abort a long index build is not verifiable from this diff because the origin/lifetime of `ctx` in `NewResourceServer` is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Postgres integration test is skipped with a silent-pass guard, potentially hiding a regression this PR introduced rather than fixing it

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a guard in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` to `t.Skip` when `dbType == "postgres"` with a TODO noting it fails in Drone but works locally. This reduces CI coverage for Postgres and can mask regressions affecting Postgres behavior introduced elsewhere in the PR, even though it’s not a runtime defect in production code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: With Init no longer called at request time, Search/History/Origin can nil-pointer or operate on an uninitialized search support if constructed via a path without eager Init, and duplicate/misleading error logs can occur, giving callers less precise errors

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `NewResourceServer` call `s.Init(ctx)` eagerly and return an error if it fails, so the claim that callers can reach `Search/History/Origin` with an uninitialized server via this constructor path is not supported by what’s shown. However, the diff does introduce duplicate/misleading error logging: `NewResourceServer` logs `"error initializing resource server"` on init failure, and `Init` itself logs the same message when `s.initErr != nil`, causing double logs for the same failure.
